newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops, Palestinians clash in West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops, Palestinians clash in West Bank.

text.p: Hundreds of stone-throwing Palestinians clashed with Israeli soldiers in the West Bank on Tuesday during protests against Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, witnesses said.
They said Israeli soldiers shot and wounded more than 25 Palestinians with rubber-coated metal bullets during clashes near the tomb of the biblical matriarch Rachel in Bethlehem.
The Voice of Palestine radio station said more than 90 other Palestinians were taken to hospital for treatment from teargas inhalation.

Israel broke ground for the construction of 6,500 housing units for Jews at Jabal Abu Ghneim, a hill of pine trees located in East Jerusalem just north of Bethlehem, last week. Israelis call the hill Har Homa.
Witnesses said that some of the Palestinian demonstrators were wearing gas masks. Some Palestinian policemen tried in vain to stop the stone-throwing. Some of the wounded were Palestinian policemen.
About 200 youths briefly clashed also with Israeli soldiers in a part of Hebron in the West Bank that is still under occupation, witnesses said. They said the soldiers refrained from firing.
An Israeli army spokeswoman confirmed the clashes in Bethlehem and said the army was using teargas to quell them.
Israel angered Palestinians last week when it went ahead with the construction despite strong international condemnation, igniting almost daily protests in the West Bank.
President Yasser Arafat's Fatah movement called on Palestinians to confront Jewish settlement activity with non-violent protests and by blocking roads used by Jewish settlers in the West Bank.
